newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Agricole regroups Indosuez, no mass layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Credit Agricole regroups Indosuez, no mass layoffs.

text.p: French bank Credit Agricole said on Thursday it would create an international investment bank force under the Banque Indosuez name involving a degree of regrouping but no straight or mass layoffs.

"Human resources management during the combination process will take place in a context of strong business and geographic complementarities between Banque Indosuez and Credit Agricole," said a statement from Caisse Nationale du Credit Agricole.

"Nevertheless, overlaps do exist and these must be managed in the interests of the group and in the respect of the staff members involved. Adjustments to the workforce, where necessary, will not lead to collective layoffs nor straight terminations."
Credit Agricole took control of Banque Indosuez in July in a agreed acquisition deal with holding company Suez that gave it 51 percent of Banque Indosuez and the option for more.

Credit Agricole chief executive Lucien Douroux told a news conference on Thursday the board of the two banks had agreed the day before on the main lines of the strategy but still had to establish the precise terms of implementation.

"The takeover of Indosuez implements further the strategy developed by Credit Agricole in 1989, strengthening its retail markets and activities and moving into new areas outside of France and in the wholesale banking business," said the news conference written statement.

"The chosen line of action is that of the creation of a wholesale banking and international pole of the Credit Agricole group. With this entity, built out of Banque Indosuez, which will keep its identity the group will hold a consistent structure of international dimensions." it said.

The regrouping will include combining CNCA's strength in cash and interest rate products with Banque Indosuez's forte in forex and overseas trading rooms in world-wide product lines "in a single trading room with unified sales forces," it said.
"Combining futures brokerage activities will enable the group to build a more efficient structure in a very competitive market where size has become a key factor," the statement said.
On the equities side, the two groups control the leading French brokers Cheuvreux de Virieu from the Banque Indosuez side with Dynabourse and Hayaux de Tilly from Credit Agricole.
"The organisational options and conditions are currently being studies," the statement said.

Douroux added: "It is obvious that an alliance is desirable for the reduction of costs and the increase of strike force". But he noted that the group had to proceed cautiously and there was no hurry given that all three brokerages were profitable and successful businesses in their own right.

In asset management, the statement spoke of combining the asset management of Segespar and Indosuez with direct links to the Caisse Nationale du Credit Agricole with nearly 650 billion francs ($128 billion) of assets under management.
Credit Agricole announced in May that it was paying around 6.3 billion francs for 51 percent of Banque Indosuez but the definitive price will be fixed in January.
It has an option to boost its stake to 80 percent from July next year and that after the year 2000 it has the possibility of buying the remaining 20 percent
-- Brian Love, Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.079 French Francs)
